paragraphs: Mi sheyyesh lo mechosh bealema vehu mitchazzeq veholek kebari, asur laasot lo shum repua apillu "y goy; abal im nachala kol gupo, o sheyyesh lo keeb gadol umitztaer kol gupo sheholek bachalishut gedola, sheqqorin bearbe "mitnachel" (mitmotet mechulsha ukeeb), "p sheholek beraglayv kenepel lemishkab dame, veshari laasot lo repua "y goy.

clarification.explanation: One who has a minor ailment and still functions as a healthy person — no medical treatment may be done for him at all, even by a gentile. But one whose entire body has become ill, or who suffers great pain and severe weakness (to the point of nearly taking to bed) — it is permitted to have a gentile treat him, even if he is still walking on his feet.
takeaways: Medical treatment by a gentile on the Sabbath is permitted only when the entire body is very ill or weak, not for a minor ailment.

paragraphs: Hachoshesh bematenayv, asur lasuk beshemen o bedabar acher lirpua; veken mi sheyyesh lo chatatin berosho, asur lasuk. vehachoshesh beshinnayv vehu holek kebari, lo yigma shekar veyiplot oto, dekevan depolet, nimtza ebed lirpua veasur; abal im keeb leh tuba demitztaer kol gupo sheholek bachalishut dehaynu "mitnachel", shari ligmoa shekar veliplot, mippene shehashshekar hu mashqeh gamur lakkol.

clarification.explanation: One who suffers pain in his back may not apply oil for treatment, and the same applies to scalp sores. One who suffers a toothache but is otherwise healthy should not gargle beer and spit it out (this is forbidden medical treatment); but one whose whole body is suffering and weak — it is permitted, since beer is an ordinary beverage.
takeaways: Gargling and spitting out beer for a toothache is forbidden for one who is otherwise ordinarily healthy; it is permitted only when weak throughout the whole body.

paragraphs: Mi sheyyesh lo mursa, dehaynu mah sheqqorin bilshon arbi "tlv" (petza muglati), o mah sheqqorin "engetzayi" (nepichut dallaqtit), sheyyesh bah lecha vedam abal hu bari, muttar liptoach otah kede shettetze hallecha vehaddam im yesh lo tzaar mizzeh; mihu, zeh davqa baenu choshesh im tissatem aach"k. veasur lidchoq beyado al hammakka, dehaynu laatzor otah kede lehotzi dam mimmenna.

clarification.explanation: One who has an abscess (a festering wound) or an inflamed swelling with fluid and blood, and is otherwise healthy — it is permitted to open it to drain the fluid if he is in distress, provided he does not mind if it closes up again afterward. It is forbidden to press on the wound by hand to draw out blood.
takeaways: Opening an abscess to relieve distress is permitted (without direct pressing to draw out blood).

paragraphs: Bemah sheqqorin bearbe "kiya" (keviyya letzorek sheibat mugla, "y hachdarat gargir apuna), muttar litten haqqitnit kede sheyyishshaer patucha, umuttar lehachalip habbeged, dei lo machlip, masrach. veyizzaher lehakin heela vehaapunin sheyyittol uqtzehen meereb-shabbat. veim yodea shemmotzi dam beqinnucha, lo yeqanneach, dehave pesiq resheh, ki zeh haddam haya balua; vekol shekken deasur lishrot habbeged bemayim kede leqannechah, yaan ki sheriyyato zehu kibbuso; veod, deatu lide sechita.

clarification.explanation: In treating a wound with a drainage wick (inserting a small pellet) — it is permitted to leave the pellet in to keep the wound open and to change the dressing (so it does not putrefy). The leaf and pellets (without their stems) should be prepared before the Sabbath. If one knows that wiping will draw blood — one should not wipe; and it is forbidden to soak the dressing in water (this is laundering, and leads to wringing).
takeaways: Treating an open wound (with a pellet to drain pus) requires advance preparation, without wiping that would draw blood and without soaking in water.

paragraphs: Etzem shennishmat, sheqqorin bearbe "pulsa" (neqa), hittir mera"n za"l lehachaziro, v"g dehammagen abraham chalaq usebira lah davqa im nishbar muttar, mishshum sakkana, abal "pulsa" bilbad en lehaqel, mikkol maqom en limchot beyad hammeqillin bazeh laasot kisbarat mera"n za"l; umihu yizzaher shello yasuk "pulsa" hannizkar beshemen. vetzipporen shepperesha rubbah dehave ketalush, muttar littela bayyad im hu mitztaer bekak. umuttar littol haqqotz bemachat, veraq yizzaher shello yotzi dam.

clarification.explanation: A dislocated bone — it is permitted to reset it (according to Maran; some are stringent when there is no danger, but one should not protest against the lenient). One should not apply oil to the dislocation. A fingernail that is mostly detached (as if already torn off) — it is permitted to remove it by hand if it causes distress. It is permitted to remove a splinter with a needle, provided it does not draw blood.
takeaways: A dislocation — permitted to reset (according to the lenient view); a mostly-detached fingernail and a splinter — permitted to remove, without drawing blood.

paragraphs: Im naasa chabbura beetzbao, asur litten beged aleha, mishshum tzobea, vekol shekken beged adom deasur. ketzad yaaseh? yannichenna bemayim qarim ad sheyyippaseq haddam; veyesh mattirin litten aleha qure akkabish, veyesh oserin. veshipshup sheosin leyige koach kede lehashib kochan alehem ulebattel ayeputan, sheqqorin bearbe "tamvuk" (issuy) - nistappequ happoseqim i chashib repua veasur, o taanug veshari.

clarification.explanation: A bruise on a finger — it is forbidden to place a cloth on it (out of concern for dyeing, especially a red cloth). One should soak it in cold water until the blood stops; some permit spiderwebs and some forbid them. Massage to strengthen tired muscles — there is doubt whether this is considered medical treatment (forbidden) or pleasure (permitted).
takeaways: A bruise — should not be covered with cloth (concern of dyeing), but rather treated with cold water; muscle massage is a halachic doubt.

paragraphs: Petila bepi-hattabbaat leitztzur, yaaseh benachat, sheyyochazenna bishte etzbeotayv bilbad veyannichenna benachat. umah sheqqorin bearbe "desatur" (choqen), asur laasoto lemi shehu atzur, veraq im napal lemishkab – shari. veasur leyisrael letaqqen petila min borit o mimmah sheqqorin bearbe "nibbet" (sukkar) lecholeh sheen bo sakkana o liladim qetannim, abal share al-yede goy shehu yetaqqen otah.

clarification.explanation: A suppository for constipation — should be inserted gently with two fingers. An enema — may not be administered for mere constipation, only if one has taken to bed. One should not prepare a suppository from soap or sugar for a patient who is not dangerously ill, or for a small child, but it is permitted through a gentile.
takeaways: A suppository for constipation is permitted, inserted gently; an enema is permitted only when one has taken to bed. Preparing a suppository from materials is permitted only through a gentile in mild cases.

paragraphs: Mi shehu bari abal margish kobed beitztomeka shello, asur lishtot shemen hannana, shezzeh en derek bene-adam lishtoto ella lirpua. veken en leekol mah sheqqorin bearbi "meiggun el vered", shehem shoshannim hambushshalim besukkar, kede laasot shilshul meat, ki gam zeh en derek leakelo ella lirpua; abal muttar lishtot mah sheqqorin bearbe "g'lb" (soda lishtiyya im me chumtzah), shehu taarobet min melach im chimmutz shel "nome" (limon), "p sheshshotehu mechamat shemmargish kobed baitztomeka shello; mippene shezzeh, derek bene-adam lishtoto letaanug tamid bekol akila.

clarification.explanation: One who is healthy but feels heaviness in the stomach — is forbidden [on the Sabbath] to drink mint oil, which people do not normally drink except for medicinal purposes; and likewise one should not eat "ma'jun al-ward" (roses cooked in sugar) to induce mild diarrhea, since this too is not normally eaten except for medicinal purposes. But it is permitted to drink "gilab" (a mixture of salt with lemon sourness), even though he drinks it because he feels heaviness in his stomach — since people normally drink it for pleasure at every meal in any case.
takeaways: A healthy person feeling stomach heaviness — forbidden on the Sabbath to use things normally taken only for medicinal purposes (mint oil, "ma'jun al-ward" for a laxative effect).
"Gilab" (salt with lemon sourness) is permitted, since people normally drink it for pleasure at every meal.

paragraphs: Asur lebari lishtot sam hamshalshel beshabbat. veishah shemmitztaeret merob chalab shebbedaddeha, muttar leqalleach baqqarqa, dekevan sheholek leibbud eno domeh ledash, abal bikli asur.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden for a healthy person to drink a laxative drug on the Sabbath. A woman suffering from an excess of milk — it is permitted for her to express it onto the ground (where it is lost, not like threshing), but forbidden into a vessel.
takeaways: A laxative drug is forbidden for a healthy person; expressing excess milk onto the ground (not into a vessel) is permitted.

paragraphs: Asur lirchotz kol gupo o rubbo bemayim chammin, vaapillu lishpok hammayim al gupo ulehishtattep asur, abal rochetz panayv yadayv veraglayv, dekol sheeno rochetz rob gupo, shari. vetzarik lehazhir bazeh hannashim bimot hachorep shettobelin belel-shabbat, vedarkam kesheyyotzein min hammayan shopekin alehem mayim chammin - sheyyishpeku raq ad chatzi gupam davqa. veken abi habben shettobel babboqer beyom-shabbat, verotzeh lishpok alayv mayim chammin kesheyyetze min hattebila, kak yaaseh. veim rotzim shettihyeh shepikat hammayim al chatzi haelyon, kaka yaasu: beod chatzi gupam hattachton omed betok hammayim o hammayan, yishpeku hammayim chammin alehem, deaz tihyeh hashshepika al chatzi gupam davqa. vy" sheapillu harochetz yadayv tzarik lizzaher shello yechammem yadayv keneged hammedura im lo yenaggebem techilla, mippene shemmapshir hammayim shealehem, venimtza kerochetz bechammin shehuchammu beshabbat baesh.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to wash the whole body or most of it in hot water, and even to pour water over it and rinse off — is forbidden; but washing only the face, hands, and feet — is permitted, since this is not most of the body. Women who immerse in the mikveh in winter should be warned that when rinsing with hot water after immersion — they should pour only up to half their body; the same applies to the father of a newborn son who immerses on the Sabbath morning and wishes to pour hot water over himself after immersion. If one wants the pouring to be specifically on the upper half, one should do so while the lower half of the body is still standing in the water or spring, and then pour hot water over the upper part. Some say that even one who washes only the hands must be careful not to warm them near a fire without first drying them, since the heat thaws the water remaining on the hands, and it turns out he is washing in water heated by fire on the Sabbath.
takeaways: Washing most of the body in hot water is forbidden on the Sabbath; only the face, hands, and feet, or half the body (carefully), is permitted.
One should also be careful not to warm wet hands near a fire without drying them first, since this is considered washing in water heated on the Sabbath.

paragraphs: Hannashim sheddarkam lirchotz penehem vesaarotehem beme-vered beshabbat kede sheyyihyeh bahem recha tob, asur lisbarat ht"z udeimmeh, daapillu bibsar haadam ikka molid recha, vekol shekken beshaar, vekol shekken kan, deepshar sheyyihyeh harecha niqlat bibgadim shellahem gam ken, debazeh asur lekulle alema; velaken asur name litten mine besamim o me veradim betok hattutin sheshshoapim bachotem kede leholid bo recha tob. veken yesh darkam lehannicha me veradim betok keli sheqqorin "qumqum" (mezallep), ukesheroim shello yesh bakkeli ella meat me veradim, mosipin alayv mayim, deasur laasot ken beshabbat, dehem kavvanatam leholid recha tob beellu hammayim asher mosipin bakkeli; abal muttar lehannicha me veradim betok "sherabbat" (mashqaot qallim) o letok maakol kede latet bo taam tob, ukemo shekkatab harab "nechpa bakkesep", vehiskim immo mahari"y ayash za"l. veken otam sherochatzim enehem beme veradim lirpua, shari, deen kavvanatam leholid recha. veken otam sheshshopekim me veradim bekappam kede leharicha, shari, deen kavvanatam leholid recha tob beyadayim shellahem, vekaasher heeleti bs"d bekol zeh bsh"q "rab-pealim".

clarification.explanation: Women who wash their face and hair with rosewater on the Sabbath (so they will have a pleasant fragrance) — this is forbidden according to the Taz and those who agree with him, since this "generates fragrance" (it generates fragrance even on human flesh, and all the more so in hair, and all the more so here where the fragrance may also be absorbed into clothing — which is forbidden according to all opinions). For the same reason it is also forbidden to put spices or rosewater into snuff ("tutin") that is inhaled through the nose in order to generate a pleasant fragrance in it; and likewise it is forbidden to add water to rosewater in a spray vessel ("kettle") when intending to generate a pleasant fragrance in the water being added. But it is permitted to add rosewater to a beverage ("sharbat") or to food in order to give it a good taste; and it is likewise permitted for one who washes his eyes with rosewater for medicinal purposes (since he does not intend to generate fragrance); and it is likewise permitted to pour rosewater into the palm of one's hand in order to smell it (since he does not intend for the fragrance to cling to his hands).
takeaways: Washing the face or hair with rosewater on the Sabbath for fragrance is forbidden ("generating fragrance," all the more so when absorbed into clothing).
It is likewise forbidden to add spices or rosewater to snuff for inhaling, or to add water to a rosewater spray vessel with fragrance in mind.
Permitted: rosewater in a beverage or food for taste, washing the eyes with it medicinally, and pouring it into the palm to smell — since none of these intend to generate or affix fragrance.

paragraphs: Yoledet, yesh lah din choleh sheyyesh bo sakkana, umechallelin aleha shabbat lehadliq lah ner, vekayyotze bishar melakot shetztzerika lahem; mihu, kol mah sheepshar laasot leshannot, osin beshinnuy. ematay niqret yoledet shemmuttar lechallel aleha shabbat? mishshettesheb al hammashber, o mishshaa shehaddam shotet, o mishshaa shechabroteha noseot otah bizrooteha sheen bah koach lahalok; vekevan shennireh bah achat meellu, mechallelin aleha shabbat beyadayim.

clarification.explanation: A woman in childbirth has the law of a critically ill patient — the Sabbath is desecrated for her (lighting a candle and the like), though with variation where possible. She is considered "in childbirth" for this purpose from the moment she sits on the birthing chair, or blood is flowing, or her companions are carrying her in their arms (too weak to walk).
takeaways: A woman in childbirth has the law of a critically ill patient from the moment she sits on the birthing chair, bleeds, or can no longer walk.

paragraphs: Kol shelosha yamim rishonim, apillu amera enah tzerika, mechallelin aleha shabbat beyadayim bedabar hatztzarik lah; abal mishshelosha vead shiba: im amera tzerika, mechallelin; veim lo amera tzerika, en mechallelin. umin shiba vead sheloshim yesh lah din choleh sheen bo sakkana, shemmuttar laasot lah al-yede goy. vehinneh poh irenu, im nitzreku lebashshel ezeh dabar leyoledet apillu beyom rishon lalleda, en mebashshelin beyadam ella "y goy, mippene sheepshar lehu behaki; al-ken tzarik lehazhiram heka dela nimtza goy, kegon shennitzreku lebashshel ezeh mashqeh ballayla sheen yekolim lehabi goy - ditzrikin lebashshel beyadayim "p haddebarim haamurim veen lachush kelal.

clarification.explanation: During the first three days after birth — the Sabbath is desecrated directly (by hand) for her needs even if she says she does not need it. From the third to the seventh day — only if she says she needs it. From the seventh to the thirtieth day — she has the law of a patient who is not dangerously ill (through a gentile only). In Baghdad, when no gentile is available (at night) — food is cooked for the new mother directly by hand even on the very first day, without concern.
takeaways: The degree of Sabbath desecration for a new mother diminishes in stages: the first 3 days (always), up to 7 (if she asked), up to 30 (only through a gentile).

paragraphs: Keshettaggia haishsha lechodesh halleda, yazminu hakkol meereb-shabbat kede shello yitztareku lechallel shabbat. veyizzaharu sheyyadliqu lah hanner beereb shabbat, sheyyihyeh bo shemen harbeh sheyyaspiq ad or habboqer.

clarification.explanation: As the month of birth approaches, everything should be prepared before the Sabbath to prevent Sabbath desecration, and one should make sure the lit candle has enough oil to last until morning.
takeaways: Preparations (including a candle with sufficient oil) should be made in advance as the month of birth approaches, to minimize Sabbath desecration.

paragraphs: Hattolesh bepiv beshabbat - ledaat rashi"y za"l yesh bazeh issur tora, veken nireh daat haramba"m za"l; mihu, battosepta (shabbat p"y) katub deen bazeh issur tora ella issur derabbanan; veal zeh sameku qetzat min haacharonim, vekaasher katabti bazeh bsh"q "rab-pealim" sham, becholeh sheyyesh bo sakkana, shehutzreku litlosh lo min hamchubbar, im yekolim litlosh bappeh yitleshu bappeh.

clarification.explanation: Plucking a plant with the mouth on the Sabbath — according to Rashi and the Rambam this carries a Torah prohibition, but according to the Tosefta this is only a rabbinic prohibition (and several later authorities relied on this). For a critically ill patient who needs something plucked from what is attached to the ground — if it is possible to pluck it with the mouth, one should do so this way (easier than plucking by hand).
takeaways: Plucking with the mouth is more lenient than plucking by hand; for a critically ill patient, plucking with the mouth is preferable when possible.

paragraphs: Shochet shebba lishchot beshabbat letzorek choleh sheyyesh bo sakkana, veyesh tarnegol qatan sheyyaspiq lecholeh, lo yishchat tarnegol gadol ella haqqatan; ken heeleti bitshuba bsh"q "rab-pealim" birayot berurot; umaskil al dabar, yimtza tob.

clarification.explanation: One who slaughters on the Sabbath for the sake of a critically ill patient, and there is a small chicken sufficient for the need — should not slaughter a large chicken, but rather the small one (to minimize the Sabbath labor performed for the patient's sake).
takeaways: Slaughtering for a critically ill patient on the Sabbath — one should choose the smallest animal sufficient for the need.
